title: Thermal-throttle spiral + dependency saturation fault-injection experiment
creator: Maya Singh
description: End-to-end chaos experiment that couples a synthetic thermal-throttle on a subset of GPU hosts with an induced dependency saturation (cache/proxy layer) to validate SLO behaviour, circuit breaker tuning, and load-shedding effectiveness during correlated degradations. Goal is to exercise graceful degradation and automated fallback policies when compute capacity and a key dependency degrade in lockstep.
hypothesis: If a small percentage (~10%) of nodes in a GPU pool enter prolonged thermal-throttled states while the L2 cache/proxy layer is saturated, our smart routing + circuit-breakers should detect degraded healthy capacity and trigger incremental load-shedding and model-fallback within the SLO window, keeping 99% P99 latency under the emergency SLO and limiting error amplification onto downstream deps.
acceptance_criteria: Automated fault injection runs without control-plane crash and completes within scheduled window

When 10-12% of GPU hosts thermal-throttle for >= 3 minutes and cache hits drop by 40%, system preserves availability: >= 99% of requests return valid responses (errors excluded) and P99 latency stays <= 3x baseline for controlled timebox
Circuit breakers detect saturated dependency within 30s and route traffic to fallback model or region according to policy
No customer-facing incidents — synthetic tenants flagged in test only; no cross-tenant bleed-through
Runbook entries produced and owners assigned for any gaps found
plan: Stage 0: Review telemetry and canary creds with SRE and runtime team
Stage 1: Prepare canary GPU pool (tagged test-pool) and synthetic tenants with traffic profiles that mirror production 95th percentile
Stage 2: Deploy thermal-throttle simulator on 10% of hosts in test-pool (kernel-level frequency clamp / simulated power cap) and validate host-level metrics
Stage 3: At t0, induce dependency saturation on cache/proxy layer by increasing request fanout from a controlled generator until 60% CPU and 40% cache-miss delta observed
Stage 4: Observe system responses (routing, cb opens, autoscaling triggers, shedding) for 10 minutes; escalate to rollback if control plane signals abnormal state
Stage 5: Run two additional variants: (A) thermal-only, (B) dep-sat-only, to compare signatures
Stage 6: Collect traces, logs, KV-cache hit/miss, kernel latency histograms, and feature-flag decisions for post-run analysis
runbook: Pre-run checklist: notify on-call, record run id in incident channel, set synthetic tenant config
Abort criteria: control-plane API error rate > 2% sustained for 60s, node pool eviction rate > 5% in 5m, or unexpected cross-tenant traffic observed
Rollback: disable throttle process across hosts and throttle down synthetic load generator; if control-plane affected, engage control-plane SRE runbook CON-CTRL-01
Post-run: rotate any test keys, collect host-level core dumps if kernel panics occurred, and run tile-based failure replay for debugging
telemetry: Dashboard: res/run/engine/p99 by tenant and model (compare baseline vs experiment)
Host metrics: GPU frequency, power, thermal temp, NVML throttling events
Dependency metrics: cache hit rate, proxy queue length, 5xx rates from dep
Routing metrics: number of fallback model invocations, per-region traffic shift, circuit-breaker open count
SLO signals: request success rate, latency percentiles, error budget burn
